newsitem.title: ITALY: Alleged killer of American boy leaves Italian jail.
newsitem.headline: Alleged killer of American boy leaves Italian jail.

text.p: One of two Italians on trial for the murder of a seven-year-old American boy which shocked Italy has been freed from prison custody, court officials said on Friday.

They said Michele Iannello, 28, had been allowed by a review tribunal to leave jail in the southern town of Catanzaro on Thursday pending a verdict in the trial over the shooting death in September 1994 of Nicholas Green.

Iannello denies involvement in the killing, for which he was arrested in November 1994, but has since turned state's evidence in other murder cases. Police took him from the jail to an undisclosed safe house, where he will live under a witness protection scheme for informers.

Nicholas was on holiday in southern Italy with his family, from Bodega Bay, California, when their hired car was chased and shot at on a motorway in a hold-up attempt. He was hit in the head as he slept on the back seat next to his sister, then four.

The family's apparent lack of rancour and their decision to donate the boy's organs, which saved the lives of six young Italians, stunned Italy and earned the Greens deep respect and admiration in the country.
La Repubblica newspaper on Friday quoted the dead boy's father, Reginald, as saying he expected justice to be done in the case. Iannello's co-accused, Francesco Mesiano, also denies involvement.

"Certainly whoever killed Nicholas is a danger to society and deserves to go to prison for a very long time. But...even Iannello and Mesiano, if they are guilty, have a soul," Green said. The next session of the trial is on November 27.
